question:
The context window contains thousands of general-knowledge questions, one per line. Each line has a User ID, which is not necessarily unique (each User ID can be associated with multiple questions). Each question has an answer that can be described as one of 6 categories: 'numeric value', 'entity', 'location', 'description and abstract concept', 'abbreviation', 'human being' — they are not explicitly labeled, so you must infer the label from the semantics of each question.

You will be asked to compute exact aggregate label statistics over pairs of users. Do not guess, estimate, or approximate the result — calculate the exact answer.

In the above data, list all pairs of user IDs (no duplicate pairs, list lower ID first) where both users have at least one instance with a numeric value or location. Each of the questions can be labelled as one of the labels (the data does not provide the labels, you need to figure out the label from the semantics of the question): description and abstract concept, entity, human being, numeric value, location, abbreviation. In your answer, list all pairs in the format (user_id_1, user_id_2), separated by newlines.

Return every matching pair as (user_id_1, user_id_2), one per line, sorted by the first user ID. If there are no matching pairs, return exactly [].
